_comment: `klt erc` supply spec for ADC_BLOCK -- the structural power-delivery
read T1 item 11 (`Power delivery (structural)`, klayout-tools#2025)
grades. Issue #330.
klt erc layout/adc-top/adc_block.gds \
layout/erc/adc_block.supply-spec.json --format json
Item 11 is the STRUCTURAL question -- `is the supply actually connected
to what it powers?` -- and nothing else. IR drop and electromigration
(`klt power`) are deliberately outside it. The pass conditions are NOT
this report's top-level `status`: they are (a) every declared supply
resolving to exactly ONE electrical island, i.e. zero
`erc.unconnected_net` and zero `erc.supply_short` naming it, and (b)
zero `erc.missing_tie` -- see TIES at the bottom. Since issue #356
BOTH halves are computed by this run, and both come back clean.
LAYER NUMBERS -- where each one comes from
Every (layer/datatype) pair below was derived from the installed PDK's
own layer table, NOT copied from another PDK's spec, and then
cross-checked against klayout-tools' curated gf180mcu deck:
* PDK:  $PDK_ROOT/gf180mcuD/libs.tech/klayout/tech/gf180mcu.lyp
(open_pdks c6d73a35f524070e85faff4a6a9eef49553ebc2b), whose
<source> entries name each drawn layer -- `Poly2 30/0@1`,
The sibling gf180mcu.map agrees for the routing stack
(`Metal1 NET,SPNET,PIN,VIA 34 0` / `Metal1 PIN 34 10`).
* klt:  klayout_tools/decks/gf180mcu.py's LAYER_NAMES table, which is
transcribed from the same upstream layer map and is what
`klt drc` renders violations against in this repo.
Both sources agree on every pair used here. They disagree with nothing;
where a name differs it is only spelling (`COMP` in the .lyp vs `Comp`
in the deck table).
STACKUP -- why each entry is here
`stackup[0]` MUST carry `role: "gate"` (`klt erc`'s own contract), so
the stack starts at Poly2 30/0 and not at Metal1. `active_layer` names
COMP 22/0, which makes gate identification and the antenna denominator
`poly n diff` rather than raw poly area (klayout-tools#1979). That
matters here for a concrete reason and not as boilerplate: ADC_BLOCK
draws two serpentine poly bodies (the comparator's load resistors,
marked RES_MK/Resistor/SAB) which are real poly with no gate oxide;
without `active_layer` they enter `gates[]` and report non-physical
antenna ratios.
Metal1 34/0 .. Metal5 81/0 are every routing layer ADC_BLOCK's merged
GDS actually draws -- verified by reading the stream, not assumed:
Metal1 1604 shapes, Metal2 1086, Metal3 1046, Metal4 1226, Metal5 1060.
MetalTop 53/0 is NOT declared because this block draws none (zero
shapes); a layer absent from the layout would not be an error, but
declaring one this block does not use would imply a coverage claim the
geometry does not support.
`label_layer` is declared ONLY on Metal1 (34/10). That is the only
layer this block's merged GDS puts ANY text on -- 84 texts on 34/10,
zero texts on every other layer, Metal5_Label 81/10 included (this
block has no top-level PDN pin text because it has no PDN: its supply
rails are drawn by the block generator, not by a place-and-route PDN
grid). Declaring 81/10 here would assert a supply-pin surface that
does not exist.
VIAS -- the stackup bridges
Contact 33/0 (Poly2<->Metal1), Via1 35/0, Via2 38/0, Via3 40/0, Via4
41/0. Note gf180mcu's via numbering is NOT monotonic with the metal it
bridges (Via3 is 40/0 and Via4 is 41/0, while Metal3 is 42/0 and Metal4
is 46/0) -- which is exactly why these are read out of the PDK's own
layer table rather than pattern-guessed.
DEVICES -- drawn bodies that are not wires (klayout-tools#2183)
`klt erc`'s connectivity model registers no devices, so any drawn
device body on a declared role conducts across its own extent. Two such
bodies exist in ADC_BLOCK and both sit directly on a declared role:
* the comparator's two poly load resistors (RES_MK 110/5, coincident
with Resistor 62/0 and SAB 49/0 in this stream) sit on Poly2 and
run rail-to-node: without this carve-out they wire `vdd` to the
comparator's preamp outputs `XCMP.pon`/`XCMP.pop`, which a run of
this same spec with `devices[]` removed reproduces directly (a
single gate net named `"XCMP.pon,XCMP.pop,vdd"`). RES_MK is the
marker klt's own gf180mcu extraction deck uses for poly-resistor
recognition, which is why it, and not the coincident Resistor/SAB,
is the layer named here.
* the CDAC's 1024 MiM unit capacitors. Their plate-to-plate bridge IS
the Via4 role's own geometry in this stream: the bottom plate is
Metal4, the top plate is FuseTop 75/0 (which this spec does not
declare as a role at all), and the 1024 Via4 shapes that land the
Metal5 strap onto FuseTop sit inside the cap. With Via4 declared as
an ordinary Metal4<->Metal5 via and no carve-out, every unit
capacitor is shorted plate-to-plate. MIM_L_MK 117/10 is the marker
(CAP_MK 117/5 is coincident with it here; the extraction deck
requires both on the top plate).
`provenance.devices[].body_area_um2` in the committed report is the
cross-check that each declaration actually bit: 300.0 um2 removed from
Poly2 and 16384.0 um2 removed from Via4. A declaration that matched
nothing would report 0.0.
What `devices[]` does NOT do is model what the device IS -- it only
stops the body being read as a wire. The device-aware read of the same
layout is `klt extract`/`klt lvs`, in layout/lvs/.
NETS -- the two declared supplies
`vdd` and `vss`, both `kind: "supply"`, which is what makes a short
between them the severe `erc.supply_short` rather than the general
`erc.multiply_driven_net`. Names are lower-case because that is what
the GDS labels say (`klt erc` matches `nets[].name` by exact string
equality against the label text, per klayout-tools docs/cli/erc.md).
Each must resolve to exactly ONE electrical island.
`erc.unconnected_net` fires on ZERO matches (nothing carries the label)
AND on MORE THAN ONE (the rail is split into pieces that never touch),
so zero findings of that rule is the affirmative `one island per
supply` verdict rather than merely an absence. This block's merged GDS
carries FOUR `vdd` labels and SIX `vss` labels -- one pair in each of
ADC_DECODE_BANK_N, ADC_DECODE_BANK_P, ADC_TOP_SW and COMPARATOR, plus
the two substrate-tie guard rings issue #356 strapped (see TIES below).
A clean run therefore says those four sub-blocks AND both guard rings
are on one rail each, which is the substantive structural claim here.
VSUBS is deliberately NOT declared, and since issue #356 for a sharper
reason than `it carries no label`. It used to be the extraction deck's
implicit substrate node, drawn nowhere. It is now a drawn, `Pplus`-
marked, contacted ring strapped to `vss`, which the deck's own
`tap_pplus` derivation claims -- so `klt extract` reports every NMOS
body on `vss` and there is no separate `VSUBS` rail left to declare at
all. See layout/erc/README.md.
TIES -- the well-tie half of item 11, now COMPUTED
This section used to be `THE ties[] OMISSION -- an absence of evidence,
not evidence of absence`, and the omission was correct while it stood:
ADC_BLOCK drew no implant layers and no well tap, so `COMP n Nplus` had
nothing to intersect and the check would have reported all 25 wells
untied whatever the layout drew. `spec/decision-records/
DR-0032-implant-layers-not-drawn.md` recorded that, and named the layout
work that would supersede it.
Issue #356 is that work. `layout/adc-top/lib/geometry.py` now draws an
`Nplus`-marked, contacted n+ tap inside every one of the 25 `Nwell`
islands and `lib/place.py` routes each one to the `vdd` trunk on a Poly2
riser; `gen_adc_top.py` closes both substrate-tie rings' `Metal1` at the
corners, marks them `Pplus`, labels them `vss` and straps them into the
block's own `vss` island. So the narrowing below is no longer vacuous --
`tap_layer: "22/0"` narrowed by `tap_requires: ["32/0"]` derives exactly
the 25 drawn tap strips and nothing else, because `Nplus` is drawn ONLY
on them (the substrate ties carry `Pplus` 31/0 instead, and no transistor
source/drain carries either -- see DR-0035).
`connect_to: "Metal1"` is the stackup role the tap has to reach, and
`net: "vdd"` is what it has to reach ON it. `klt erc` wires the derived
tap region to that role in its own connectivity model and then probes
each well's tap for the declared net, so ZERO `erc.missing_tie` here is
the affirmative `every drawn well is tapped AND the tap reaches vdd`
verdict -- both halves, not just the first.
WHAT KEEPS THAT FROM BEING VACUOUS IN THE OTHER DIRECTION. A check that
reports zero findings is only evidence if it could have reported some.
Two committed controls under `controls/` establish that it could:
* `adc_block.tie-wrong-implant.control.json` declares the SAME tie with
`tap_requires: ["31/0"]` -- Pplus, the substrate-tie implant, which
this stream really does draw but never inside a well. The derived tap
region is non-empty and simply lands nowhere the check is looking, so
all 25 wells report `erc.missing_tie`. That is the discriminating
control the pre-#356 `tie-narrowed` reproduction could not be: it
fails for a reason that depends on WHERE the implant is drawn, so it
would go green if the taps were marked wrongly.
* `adc_block.tie-bare.known-gap.json` is unchanged and still
reproduces klayout-tools#2199's degenerate-declaration skip: a bare
`tap_layer: "22/0"` matches every source/drain contact in the well
and `klt erc` refuses to grade it. It is the reason the narrowing is
mandatory rather than cosmetic.
VSUBS, again. The `nets[]` note above still declines to declare `VSUBS`,
and for a sharper reason than before: since #356 the substrate is not an
undrawn implicit node at all -- it is a drawn, `Pplus`-marked, contacted
ring strapped to `vss`, which is why `klt extract` now reports every NMOS
body on `vss` instead of on the deck's synthesized `vsubs` global. There
is no separate `VSUBS` rail left to declare.
